checks.name: forced_401
checks.detail: Re-run live against devx after the gateway_401_remap fix. Tampered the last 6 characters of the idToken JWT signature segment in localStorage, left the cookie and other tokens untouched, then triggered authenticated calls via the app's own nav (client-side route to /applications). Checked via performance.getEntriesByType('resource'). Every authenticated call now returns status 401 (previously 403 ACCESS_DENIED, see the superseded evidence file). Sanity-checked the fix also holds for a syntactically-malformed bearer token (still 401 UNAUTHORIZED, unaffected/unrelated code path) via raw curl against the live API.

checks.name: refresh_exactly_once
checks.detail: Re-run live against devx three times after both fixes. Root cause of the original failure (documented in the superseded evidence file) was NOT only the 403-vs-401 status code: src/frontend/api/client.ts's setAuthContext() was never called anywhere in the app outside tests, so the interceptor's authContext was permanently stuck at a stub that immediately rejected ('AuthContext not initialised') without ever calling Cognito or clearing state. Fixed via auth_context_wiring (commit e32e25b). After both fixes, three separate live tamper-and-navigate runs all produced the correct, complete terminal state: all CognitoIdentityServiceProvider.* localStorage keys cleared, the cognito_id_token cookie cleared, and a redirect to /login - i.e. a genuine forced sign-out, not the previous dead-end 'ACCESS_DENIED'/'Request failed' banner with stale tokens. The exact intermediate network sequence (one refresh attempt, one retry, one final 401, then signOut) could not be captured mid-flight via the remote browser automation tool - the full cycle completes faster than the tool's own round-trip latency allows a mid-sequence snapshot. This is corroborated instead by: (a) the interceptor code's _retry flag, which structurally caps retries at exactly one before falling through to authContext.signOut() (src/frontend/api/client.ts:84-98, unchanged by this fix), and (b) the existing unit test test_p07_401_contract_still_refreshes_once (tests/integration/api-client.test.ts), which asserts mockRefreshSession is called exactly once and mockSignOut is called, in this exact scenario, and passes. Because the real Cognito SDK's local getSession() judges the tampered-but-unexpired idToken as not locally expired, refreshSession() resolves with the SAME bad token rather than fetching a new one over the network (no separate refresh-token network call is observed or expected for this specific failure mode - a bad signature, not a genuinely expired token) - the single retry with that same token then fails again, correctly triggering signOut(). A genuinely expired (not just tampered) token would instead be silently refreshed even earlier, inside getCurrentToken()/getSession() itself, before ever reaching the interceptor - a separate, already-passing code path per the 1.6 handoff's own 'known nuance' note.
checks.status: PASS - fixed by auth_context_wiring (commit e32e25b); terminal state (cleared storage + redirect to login) reproduced on 3/3 live runs post-fix
